title: document.cookie implementations don't match the spec
body:
https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#dom-document-cookie

> The cookie attribute represents the cookies of the resource identified by the document's URL\.

> On getting [...] the user agent must return the cookie-string for the document's URL for a "non-HTTP" API, decoded using UTF-8 decode without BOM.

It looks like current UAs don't implement `document.cookie` exactly as described on the spec: the [document's URL](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#the-document's-address) may be changed using `history.replaceState` but on Firefox and Chrome this doesn't affect the value of `document.cookie`.

For example:
1. Navigate to http://example.com/pathA/
2. Set a cookie for path /pathB/ (e.g. run `document.cookie = "test=ok; path=/pathB/"`)
3. Change the document's URL to http://example.com/pathB/ (`history.replaceState(null, "", "/pathB/")`)

Now, as per spec `document.cookie` should give `test=ok` but on Firefox and Chrome we are not able to retrieve the content of the `test` cookie.

I know that cookie's [path "isolation" isn't a security feature](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6265#section-8.5) and there are means of retrieving cookies meant for a different path, but I think that the behaviour of Firefox and Chrome is the right one and the spec should be corrected to match it.

I haven't tested this on other browsers.

What do you think?

Should 
> document's [relevant settings object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#relevant-settings-object)'s [creationURL](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-environment-creation-url)

be used instead of 

> document's URL

?
